about: Passages of the team's V16 Word documents behind study lines for papers the documents cite (30 October 2026). Each is verbatim in the named document; verify with tools/check_compact_evidence_documents.py <V16 folder>.

17941009.quote: Johns Hopkins, 22 synchronous hepatic resections (17 pancreatic, 5 other periampullary).
Results: Median survival 5.9 vs 5.6 months with bypass alone.
Gleisner 2007 · synchronous liver metastases Abstract only; full text pending.

18669451.quote: Single centre, 47 hepatectomies with lymphadenectomy. Nodes after chemotherapy.
Results: 5-year survival 25% pedicular vs 0% coeliac or para-aortic.

21937390.quote: Single-centre series, 20 transplants. Nodal invasion recorded.
Results: Nodal invasion an independent predictor of death.

22047762.quote: Supports established LDLT expertise and donor-recipient double equipoise; informed donor evaluation remains independent of recipient benefit.
LDLT section describes considering an observation period such as 3 months to assess tumor behavior. It does not establish a universally mandatory minimum 3 months for every HCC LDLT candidate.
Immunosuppression conclusions predate the completed SiLVER trial and modern ICI cohorts.

23532111.quote: Japanese national survey, 14,872 resections. 112 with pathologically proven nodal metastasis.

23737695.quote: Cancer Care Ontario guideline (archived December 2020; evidence to January 2010). Liver and lung metastases.

Results: Combined or staged metastasectomy recommended when all lung metastases can be removed; liver resection may follow a prior lung resection; routine liver resection not recommended with portal nodal disease.

24384494.quote: 2012 London multidisciplinary consensus with systematic searches through October 2012, published 2014; not a new LT cohort.
LT recommendations rest on low-quality observational evidence. The paper explicitly says proposed NET selection criteria were not prospectively validated; downstaging had not been assessed.
Historical LT section lists poor differentiation, non-portal primary, extrahepatic disease except perihilar nodes, and severe carcinoid heart disease among exclusions.
therapeutic discussion predates CLARINET, NETTER-1, CABINET and modern WD G3/NEC differentiation.

25789941.quote: LiverMetSurvey registry. 149 liver plus lung resections vs 9,185 liver-only.
Results: Adjusted 5-year survival 44.5% vs 51.5%; 14.3% when lung disease was not resected.

26555945.quote: In the SiLVER randomized trial (n = 525, randomized 4-6 weeks post-transplant) the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival was NOT met: 64.5% without sirolimus versus 70.2% with sirolimus (p = 0.28; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.62-1.15). Overall survival also did not differ (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.58-1.13). A benefit was apparent only across the first 3-5 years. The greater apparent benefit in low-risk (within-Milan) recipients and in recipients aged 60 or under comes from exploratory subgroup analyses that were neither powered nor corrected for multiplicity
Open-label international randomized immunosuppression trial: 525 LT recipients with HCC randomized at 4–6 weeks after LT, 264 mTOR-free versus 261 sirolimus-containing.

27017160.quote: Meta-analysis, 52 studies, 15,144 patients (2,308 with extrahepatic disease). Synchronous or previous extrahepatic disease resected with the liver.
Results: 5-year survival: lung 26% (15–39%), peritoneum 17%, nodes 15%; R0 at both sites lowered the risk of death (RR 0.73).
Limits: Nodal locations pooled; selected series.

27647626.quote: Prospective A2ALL-2 interviews: 271/297 eligible donors, before and through 24 months after donation.

Cumulatively 75% reported nonmedical out-of-pocket expenses, 45% lost wages, 37% uncovered medical expenses and 44% burdensome costs at ≥1 assessment. Burden was 39.6% at three months (99/250) and 19.4% at two years (27/139).
Do not infer: Self-report, variable denominators, administrative censoring/attrition, English-only selected donors and two-year horizon.

27777223.quote: CONSORT pilot principles are adapted here, not a direct validation of single-arm transplant trial design.

27856064.quote: Heidelberg, 128 M1 resections. Preoperative therapy and response selection not described in the abstract.
Hackert 2016 · M1 resection Abstract only; full text pending.

28009741.quote: MSKCC, 219 hepatectomies with resected extrahepatic disease. Synchronous disease, resected within 6 months.
Results: Portal vs retroperitoneal nodes: no survival difference (p=0.768); incomplete extrahepatic resection: no survivors beyond 3.5 years; disease-free at 10 years 3.2%.

28230639.quote: 2018 narrative review of general LT mTOR immunosuppression; not a NET/CRLM antirecurrence trial.

Reported result: H2304 randomized 719 general LT recipients; everolimus plus reduced tacrolimus from day 30 improved estimated renal function versus standard tacrolimus. Review reports 80.9 versus 70.3 mL/min/1.73m2 at one year and discontinuation 25.7% versus 14.1%.
Review describes SiLVER HCC primary endpoint as negative
Several cited results were conference abstracts; no new independent trial data.

28513896.quote: Spolverato 2017 · recurrence after NELM surgery Abstract only; full text pending.

28516291.quote: Verona, 24 of 535 metastatic PDAC. Disappearance of liver metastases and CA19-9 fall.
Frigerio 2017 · downstaged metastatic PDAC Abstract only; full text pending.

28573685.quote: Retrospective Mayo cohort of 124 pCCA recipients after neoadjuvant treatment and LT, 2004–2013
This is an infection cohort, not a randomized immunosuppression trial.
These are nonrandomized associations, not proof that LDLT causes infection.
Single center, historical practice, confounding by technical complexity and complications.

28858392.quote: Single centre, 74 locally advanced iCCA. Locally advanced, not metastatic.
Results: 39 (53%) resected after chemotherapy, median survival 24.1 months (similar to upfront resection).

29196022.quote: Meta-analysis, 885 patients. Primary resection with unresectable liver metastases.
Partelli 2017 · primary resection meta-analysis Abstract only; full text pending.

29480952.quote: In Toronto, 11/18 treated patients (61%) dropped out, six received LT and one remained waiting.
Prospective Toronto program, 2009–2015: 43 referred, 24 assessed in detail, 18 treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiation, six transplanted and one still awaiting LT.
ITT median OS was 16.4 months, with one-/two-year OS 70.6%/35.3%. Post-LT one-/two-year OS was 83.3%/55.6%.
Only one of six explants had pCR.
Very small single-center series, substantial all-pathway attrition, short recipient follow-up
median recipient follow-up was only 12.6 months.

29560571.quote: Single centre, 55 cytoreductions with extrahepatic disease. 87% combined intra- and extrahepatic.
Chan 2018 · cytoreduction with EHD Abstract only; full text pending.

30218247.quote: Results: Extrahepatic metastasis HR 3.9 for death.
Limits: Not split by treated vs untreated.
Xiang 2018 · NF-NELM resection Abstract only; full text pending.

30568386.quote: Supports comprehensive staging, MDT review and consideration of surgery/ablation for technically treatable oligorecurrence with adequate organ reserve.
Selected resection series report median survival approximately 28–65 months versus 5–15 months with systemic treatment only, but the review explicitly acknowledges major selection bias
Older systemic-treatment era; do not import the paper's sorafenib-only pathway into a 2026 algorithm.
The review overstates some mTOR prevention conclusions relative to the long-term primary SiLVER endpoint

30610789.quote: Systematic review, 16 studies. Metastasectomy of pancreatic and periampullary cancer.
Results: Ampullary primaries and isolated pulmonary recurrence had better prognosis.

30636895.quote: SEER, 346 metastatic ampullary cancers. Primary-tumor resection; no metastatic-site or response data.
Results: Matched median survival 16 vs 8 months; association strongest without chemotherapy (selection).
Limits: Cannot support metastasectomy after response.

31818843.quote: CSPAC-1 randomized trial protocol. ≤3 liver foci; randomization requires SD/PR and CA19-9 fall >50% to <500 U/mL.

32280473.quote: Single-centre cohort, 55 resections; distant metastasis excluded. Nodal metastasis in 11 (20%).
Results: Nodal metastasis: survival HR 6.95 (2.15–22.44); local extrahepatic invasion HR 4.91; 5-year survival 16.4% overall.
Limits: Small; survival by nodal status shown only as curves and hazard ratios, without numeric rates.

32573905.quote: Comparison of 64 patients with extrahepatic recurrence and controlled liver disease. Nodes, adrenal, peritoneum, lung or brain; resectable.
Results: 5-year survival 60.5% with resection vs 9.1% without.

32671802.quote: Narrative Mayo expert review with an updated 349-entry/211-LT program experience from 1993–2018; extensive overlap with prior Mayo reports, not an independent validation cohort.
Reported ITT one-/five-/ten-year survival was 80%/51%/46%; corresponding recipient survival was 91%/69%/62%. PSC and de novo outcomes differ substantially and should not be pooled without context.
Reported late arterial and portal-venous complication risks justify transplant vascular planning and surveillance.
Expert narrative, overlapping center data, treatment-era and selection effects, no randomized comparison

32787474.quote: Meta-analysis, 9 studies, 746 patients. Peritoneal disease with vs without liver metastases.
Results: Overall survival HR 1.68 with liver metastases.

33079246.quote: Single centre, 410 resected extrahepatic CCA. 16 with para-aortic metastasis resected.
Results: Median survival 33.7 vs 16.7 months (resected vs unresected); not worse than regional node-positive.
Limits: Very small; perihilar and distal mixed.

33908381.quote: In Sposito et al., 32 patients with recurrence and at least 6 months of postrecurrence follow-up had median recurrence latency 82.9 months and 5-/10-year survival from recurrence of 76.3%/45.5%.
The seven early-recurrence cases (within 24 months) had five-year postrecurrence OS 0% versus 89.5% in 25 later recurrences
surgery versus other treatment was associated with 5-year postrecurrence survival of 90.9% versus 64.5% (P=.062), an unadjusted, non-significant overall comparison.
Selection, late-recurrence biology and resectability materially confound the results.

35740555.quote: Historical single-center retrospective cohort, 1988–2022: 67 LT recipients (37 pCCA, 17 iCCA, 13 mixed HCC-CCA); 44 recurred.
Median post-recurrence OS was 16.7 months with RIM versus 5.3 months without it. Absence of RIM was associated with worse survival in the adjusted model (HR 4.19, 95% CI 1.29–13.58).
mTOR treatment before or after recurrence did not show an independent survival association.
Small, nonrandomized, >30-year mixed-disease cohort; treatment selection and performance-status confounding; RIM not standardized

35758505.quote: Heidelberg, 173 explored after chemotherapy for metastatic PDAC. RECIST PR/CR of metastases plus a fall in CA19-9 and CEA, usually ≥6 cycles.
Results: 93 resected (45 ypM0); median survival 25.5 vs 10.7 vs 8.1 months; CA19-9 ≥400 HR 2.31; surgery ≥9 months after diagnosis HR 1.82.
Counsel: in Heidelberg, 46% were unresectable at exploration and only about 1 in 4 explored was ypM0; median survival 25.5 months (ypM0) vs 10.7 (ypM1) vs 8.1 (exploration only).
Limits: Single referral centre; no intention-to-treat denominator.

36160651.quote: No validated post-LT adjuvant anticancer regimen was established
Selection of later, limited, surgically accessible recurrence confounds treatment comparisons.

37208566.quote: Mayo, 546 cytoreductive hepatectomies. Extrahepatic distant metastases in 16% (peritoneum, bone).
Results: Associated with worse overall survival, not progression-free survival; median survival 122 months overall.

37433437.quote: NCCN ampullary guideline. Systemic therapy in all stages.
Results: “Select tumors may be treated surgically.”
Every criterion drawn from OPTN policy, drug labelling, NCCN or a device authorisation must be re-verified against the current source before any use.

37555110.quote: Nine-centre cohort, 111 transplant recipients with cHCC–CC. Diagnosis on explant; nodal metastasis in 3.
Results: Recurrence 44.1% vs 19.1% in HCC; first recurrence extrahepatic-only in 37 of 49.
Limits: Nodal signal rests on 3 patients.

37760542.quote: after LT, do not automatically use the nontransplant ICI combinations because of rejection and graft-loss risk.
After LT, do not automatically apply the nontransplant ICI matrix. Rejection and graft-loss risk require transplant/oncology assessment and an explicit exceptional-use decision

37890597.quote: Dutch nationwide screening cohort, 75 patients. Any malignant node precludes further screening.
Results: EUS sampling found malignant nodes in 3 of 75; surgical staging found non-regional malignant nodes in 6 of 43.

37986552.quote: A meta-analysis of 15 studies/315 recipients estimated explant pCR at 32% (95% CI 19–49), with substantial heterogeneity and some mixed iCCA populations.
Mayo subgroup pCR was 46% (31–61), SBRT 9% (1–44), and other regimens 33% (13–63).
Study-level pCR was not associated with OS in meta-regression.
Transplanted-only selection; mixed pCCA/iCCA populations; small and nonrandomized regimen subgroups; center overlap addressed imperfectly; ecological meta-regression

38055245.quote: Narrative review; no new patient cohort or meta-analysis.
Reported result: Useful historical synthesis, not a substitute for current allocation guidance or primary trial denominators.
The paper says no iCCA/CRLM MELD exceptions and uses older allocation sources: outdated for 2026.
NET ELTR sentence p 216 reverses pre-/post-2000 five-year OS (46% versus 59%)
SECA-II DFS labels p 215 use 1/3/5 years although the primary paper reports 1/2/3 years

38467379.quote: Phase II trial, 40 patients with controlled HCC and 1–5 metastases. Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to all metastases.

38679630.quote: 15-centre cohort, 150 patients with extrahepatic metastases whose intrahepatic tumor reached partial or complete response (mRECIST). Only 8 of 26 operated patients had their metastases removed; 85% had partial (not complete) response of extrahepatic disease.
Results: Median survival 16.5 vs 11.3 months from response (surgery vs none); progression-free survival not different.
Limits: Immortal-time bias; operated patients more often oligometastatic; counts inconsistent.

38721015.quote: Unplanned interim safety/feasibility analysis of TransMet RCT; 157 evaluated, 94 randomized, 47 per arm, 38 protocol-LT recipients.

38/47 reached LT after median 51 days; nine did not, including three occult metastatic nodes at laparotomy and one new prostate cancer. Eighty-one percent feasibility applies to selected/randomized candidates, not all screened.
Three of 38 retransplanted; one of 38 postoperative deaths.
Unplanned interim analysis, incomplete long-term endpoint reporting

38822227.quote: Japan–Korea multicentre, 56 conversion operations (biliary). Locally advanced.

39274193.quote: California registry, 327 with extrahepatic disease. Nodes not counted as extrahepatic.

Results: Liver resection (n=23): 5-year survival 78%; non-surgical liver-directed therapy median survival 13 vs 16 months with none (not formally compared; the authors read liver-directed therapy favourably).

39299553.quote: Weighted comparison, 209 patients with lung oligometastases. Metastasectomy vs stereotactic radiotherapy.
Results: 2-year local control 98.2% vs 97.0% (unweighted); weighted 2-year progression-free survival 23.0% vs 24.7%.

39524972.quote: Japanese expert consensus on oncological resectability (17 panelists). Statement 9 (15/17): extrahepatic spread is basically BR2; localized spread could be BR1 (solitary node at station 3, 8 or 12; P1 peritoneum; unilateral adrenal; few lung metastases).
Limits: Surgeon-only panel; a classification, not a treatment recommendation; permissive (“could be”); no response or interval criteria.

39547997.quote: Narrative review with descriptive JLTS LDLT registry data; 16 NET recipients, 14 transplanted in/before 2007, none after 2012.
four of 16 died within 90 days; median OS 58.4 months, five-year OS 50%.
Historical Japanese series does not prove current LDLT safety or superiority

39671534.quote: Median OS was 14.0 versus 13.6 months (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.72–1.14; P=0.41); PFS was 7.5 versus 6.3 months
Of 452 randomized, 441 eligible participants were analyzed
The iCCA subgroup had median OS 13.5 versus 13.6 months

39834127.quote: Narrative CRLM review; eight distinct primary cohorts plus overlapping follow-ups/cross-trial comparisons.
CEA 80 and lesion size 5.5 cm are prognostic associations
Table 1 simultaneously lists stable disease as inclusion and exclusion for TransMet
Table 2 reverses the direction of the <2-year timing risk. Do not copy table rules blindly.

39915735.quote: METAPANC randomized trial protocol. ≤3 liver metastases, no extrahepatic disease; 8 cycles mFOLFIRINOX; CR, PR or stable disease randomized.

39918658.quote: Meta-analysis and pooled patient data, 466 patients (49.6% iCCA). Of 55 iCCA, 19 had metastatic disease before conversion, mostly nodal; most series are locally advanced only.
Results: Conversion associated with longer survival than non-surgical care (HR 0.39)
Limits: Case-report-based pooled data; strong selection.

39939239.quote: Retrospective Houston Methodist cohort, 2008–2023: 53 LT recipients, 27 pCCA and 26 iCCA
The optimized conventional Cox association between mTOR use and OS was HR 0.16 (0.06–0.45; p=.001). It was not confirmed when mTOR exposure was treated as time-dependent: OS HR 0.52 (0.19–1.43; p=.2)
Small, heterogeneous, nonrandomized cohort; stepwise model selection; post-LT exposure timing; overlapping Houston patients.
mTOR exposure starts after LT, creating an important timing/immortal-time problem in simple ever-treated comparisons.

40075720.quote: Single centre, 20 conversions of biliary cancer. 5 with para-aortic nodes; all 5 were negative on para-aortic sampling at conversion resection (in 3 the nodes had disappeared on imaging).
Results: One pCCA patient (para-aortic nodes cleared) had axial nodal recurrence 11 months after conversion.
Single centre, 101 unresectable biliary cancers; 20 converted. 14 converted had distant disease (liver 6, para-aortic nodes 5, peritoneal 3).
Results: 5-year survival 55.0% with conversion vs 8.6% without, from the start of chemotherapy; recurrence 14 of 20.
Limits: Mixed biliary subsites; immortal-time bias; not iCCA-specific; the abstract gives 65.0% vs 4.3%, inconsistent with the text.

40084343.quote: Meta-analysis, 9 studies, 467 patients with lung metastases. Mostly metachronous after pancreatectomy; chemotherapy before lung resection uncommon.
Results: Pooled HR 0.637 (0.531–0.764); significant publication bias; survival from pancreatectomy.

40105312.quote: Nationwide Japanese study, 1,509 borderline-resectable HCC. BR1 as defined by the 2023 consensus, which includes localized extrahepatic spread; the number with extrahepatic spread is not given in the abstract.
Limits: No extrahepatic subgroup in the abstract.

40317676.quote: Results: Nodes beyond the hepatoduodenal, common hepatic artery and peripancreatic area: median survival 13.3 vs 24.3 months (p=0.047).
Kurimoto 2025 · iCCA nodal metastasis areas Abstract only; full text pending.

40372590.quote: Meta-analysis, 17 studies, 988 patients. Synchronous peritoneal and liver metastases.
Results: CRS/HIPEC with liver treatment: 5-year survival 37%.

40808313.quote: Supports individualized ICI use, acknowledgement of rejection, infection/decompensation and anti-VEGF wound-healing risk
Some categorical statements exceed the cited evidence

40844852.quote: Statement 25: basiliximab may permit delayed CNI initiation for renal recovery (Weak, Level 2); statement 26 advises against ATG induction (Strong, Level 2).
Statement 32 only suggests mTOR use for HCC WITHIN Milan to improve RFS up to three years (Weak, Level 3). It does not establish NET/CRLM recurrence reduction
Not a 2026 literature search: substantive search update ended September 2024.
Most immunosuppression and cancer evidence is indication-specific; do not extrapolate HCC benefit causally to NET/CRLM.

40889502.quote: Conversion studies such as TransGOLP address a different population; neither establishes LT efficacy or post-LT ICI safety.

41056563.quote: Adult HCC-exception candidates listed during 2016–January 2024; 8,367 total: 5,472 TACE and 2,895 TARE.

TARE was associated with lower waitlist dropout: adjusted subdistribution HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.74–0.93).; Odds of complete pathologic necrosis were greater after TARE: OR 2.24 (95% CI 1.88–2.67).; No significant overall-survival difference: adjusted HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.85–1.03)
Residual confounding by center, era, technical suitability, tumor burden and access; selecting sole-modality recipients excludes treatment switchers

41063730.quote: US national cancer database, 4,329 patients on first-line immunotherapy. 138 (3.2%) had curative treatment afterwards, including 15 with distant and 10 with nodal metastasis.
Results: Propensity-matched HR 0.22 (0.14–0.33) for death with curative treatment.
Limits: Immortal-time bias; curative intent uncertain; modality not separated for the 15 distant and 10 nodal patients.
Results: Curative treatment after immunotherapy associated with longer survival (propensity-matched HR 0.22 in the main text).
Limits: Immortal-time and indication bias; no response or recurrence data; cannot inform transplantation after treated extrahepatic disease.

41366165.quote: Single centre, 118 with synchronous liver metastases. Asymptomatic pNET.
Results: Primary resection did not change survival (median 10 years); extrahepatic disease predicted progression.
Podrascanin 2025 · pNET with liver metastases Abstract only; full text pending.

41405235.quote: The recurrent HCC/CCA disease-specific management domain is explicitly outside this cancer-screening section

41490475.quote: Radiologic objective response: 195/338 lesions; pooled 61.2% (95% CI 44.6–75.6).
Low/very-low certainty, small heterogeneous nonrandomized cohorts and recipient selection. No demonstrated superiority over ablation, TACE or TARE.

41720193.quote: Post-LT ICI carries a distinct graft-loss risk and is not routine recurrence therapy.

41780001.quote: Open-label randomized phase 2–3 trial at 11 Chinese hospitals; 178 patients randomized to neoadjuvant GOLP (n=88) or immediate surgery (n=90)
Median EFS was 18.0 versus 8.7 months (P<0.001); 24-month EFS was 37% versus 25%.
At interim analysis, 24-month OS was 79% versus 61% (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.23–0.79; P=0.005), which did NOT meet the prespecified interim OS significance boundary of P=0.0019.
Highly fit resectable population; median follow-up 16.9 months and interim OS analysis. This was neither a conversion-to-transplant trial nor an allograft-safety study.

41785904.quote: International Delphi consensus. ≤3 lesions in one organ (liver or lung) reached only relative majority (58% and 42%); systemic therapy before local treatment in synchronous disease (82%).
Results: No induction duration or response thresholds defined.

41986186.quote: Reports 23 studies and 6,318 patients, principally retrospective post-LT cohorts
no pooled estimate or validated program-quality trigger is calculated.
the review does not prove equivalence or establish a quantitative safe expansion boundary.
Internal flow/count inconsistencies, missing study sample counts/outcome estimates, variable definitions and reliance on retrospective cohorts limit reproducibility.

42073607.quote: AASLD 2023 actually recommends discontinuation at least 3 months before LT
Guideline attribution errors, mixed eligibility/interventions, overlapping datasets and inconsistent denominators substantially weaken its use for protocol thresholds.
Claim that >50 days normalizes rejection versus non-ICI controls overstates the 119-recipient source, which lacks a parallel non-ICI control group.

42081099.quote: Japan Pancreas Society, 90 conversion operations. Median 10.4 months of chemotherapy.
Hashimoto 2026 · Japan Pancreas Society conversion Abstract only; full text pending.

42153585.quote: Retrospective three-center German study, 2002–2021: 19 incidental biliary tract cancers found on explant versus 140 HCC recipients within Milan criteria.
Five-year OS was 65% in incidental BTC versus 73% in HCC (p=.31); DFS 54% versus 69% (p approximately .25). Failure to reject a difference is not proof of equivalence.

Incidental tumors without pre-LT suspicion, mixed anatomic sites, tiny sample, selection/era confounding and underpowered survival comparisons. Not evidence for intentional transplantation of known advanced iCCA or pCCA.

42169873.quote: SEER, 256 metastatic iCCA; matched 68 pairs. No response or metastatic-site data.
Results: 3-year survival 13.8% with surgery vs 3% without.

42294332.quote: Supports the practical scheduling advantage of LDLT for coordinating an ICI-free interval, while explicitly stating that rejection risk is not eliminated.
Narrative ranges are not independent estimates and must be replaced by source-specific primary denominators for consent.
PDF p 3 wrongly describes Natarajan's 311 candidate cohort as 311 transplant recipients

42488112.quote: Single-center retrospective descriptive series of 25 selected transplant recipients after ICI
Table 2 identifies 17 HCC, seven iCCA and one pCCA recipient. No all-treated or referred-patient denominator and no comparator are supplied.
Four HCC recurrences and four HCC deaths were reported. No CCA recurrence or death was reported at available follow-up
two hepatic acute-rejection events, one rejection of a concurrently transplanted kidney, and one immediate liver graft failure requiring retransplantation
The aggregate statement assigning all rejection to HCC conflicts with case 23 and Table 2. The authors' approximate four-week washout suggestion is not a validated safe threshold

42524843.quote: 55-centre cohort, 219 locally advanced biliary cancers. No distant disease.
Results: 24 (10.9%) resected after systemic therapy; median survival 22.5 vs 19.9 months.
Rimini 2026 · locally advanced BTC Abstract only; full text pending.

42804100.quote: Single centre, 143 with intraoperative para-aortic sampling. Upfront surgery.
Results: Para-aortic metastasis in 17 (11.9%); PET identified only 17.6%; with para-aortic metastasis, survival did not differ with or without resection (15.6 vs 18.0 months, p=0.790).

42882932.quote: Single centre, 110 pCCA; 72 received neoadjuvant gemcitabine–S-1. Regional nodes defined by FDG-PET uptake only; distant disease excluded.
Results: Curative resection 85.1%, 65.8% and 24.0% in resectable, borderline and locally advanced groups.
Limits: No survival for node-positive patients; benefit not established.

42905970.quote: PANODE, 212 ampullary resections. Upfront surgery; adjuvant therapy in 4%.
PANODE prospective cohort, 1,218 resections. Station 16b1 sampled at upfront surgery.
Results: PDAC 16b1-positive median survival 10 vs 24 months (aHR 2.33); authors advise against aborting resection on 16b1 alone.
